summary: Windows + PowerShell production-readiness review focused on package managers, lockfiles, runtime/dev dependencies, supply-chain verification, package scripts, version consistency, and dependency auditability.
active_objective: Make dependency and supply-chain state production-ready without installing, updating, removing, or changing packages.
assumptions: Target runtime is Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11 with PowerShell 7.
Frontend package manager is npm because src\OnlyRag.Web contains package.json and package-lock.json and no pnpm, Yarn, or Bun lockfiles.
.NET dependencies are resolved by SDK-style csproj PackageReference entries; no NuGet lockfile or central package management file is present.
OCR runtime package sets are controlled by scripts\ocr\requirements*.txt and scripts\ocr\runtime-manifest.json.
Bundled Qdrant runtime is controlled by packaging\qdrant\manifest.json.
current_tasks: Enable NuGet dependency lockfiles for the solution so production restores are deterministic and reviewable.
Run NuGet vulnerability audit after a controlled restore: dotnet list .\OnlyRag.sln package --vulnerable --include-transitive.
Pin the npm CLI version used for production builds by adding an explicit package manager policy in the appropriate project metadata or tooling.
Audit all npm runtime and dev dependencies from package-lock.json before release, including install-script packages esbuild, fsevents, and Playwright transitive fsevents.
Add a Python OCR supply-chain verification policy for scripts\ocr\requirements*.txt because packages are version-pinned but not hash-pinned.
Verify OCR package availability from the declared indexes for each supported Python version before release.
Prepare and verify the Qdrant payload from packaging\qdrant\manifest.json before packaging; the local payload is currently absent.
Document and enforce allowed package sources for npm, NuGet, Python OCR indexes, and Qdrant downloads in the release gate.
next_tasks: Run the canonical gate after dependency lock and source policy work is complete: pwsh .\scripts\Invoke-Gate.ps1 -Configuration Release.
Run installer-inclusive verification after Qdrant payload preparation: pwsh .\scripts\Invoke-Gate.ps1 -Configuration Release -IncludeInstaller.
Review CI tool setup for exact SDK/package-manager alignment with local production builds.
Generate a release dependency inventory for .NET packages, npm packages, Python OCR packages, and bundled Qdrant.
blockers: NuGet vulnerability status is not verifiable from the current clean workspace without restore assets or NuGet lockfiles; dotnet list .\OnlyRag.sln package --vulnerable --include-transitive --no-restore fails because project.assets.json files are absent.
NuGet restore is not locked, so production restore can change transitive package resolution.
Qdrant production payload is absent under packaging\qdrant\payload, so packaging depends on fetching the manifest-pinned external asset before release.
risks: package.json does not declare a packageManager field, so npm version selection relies on the developer or CI environment even though package-lock.json is present.
package-lock.json uses lockfileVersion 3 with 292 package entries; npm audit currently reports no vulnerabilities, but install-script packages need explicit release review.
Runtime npm dependencies use semver ranges in package.json while package-lock.json pins resolved versions; production installs must use npm ci only.
.NET PackageReference versions are direct and exact, but transitive dependency resolution is not committed without packages.lock.json.
Python OCR requirements pin versions but do not pin hashes and use an extra PaddlePaddle package index for GPU runtimes.
Qdrant download is constrained to GitHub/raw.githubusercontent.com HTTPS URLs and SHA256-checked by script, but build/package steps still depend on external availability when payload is missing.
CI uses actions/setup-node with node-version lts/* while package.json accepts ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0; exact production Node major should be fixed for release reproducibility.
CI uses actions/setup-dotnet 10.0.x while global.json pins 10.0.300 with latestFeature roll-forward; release builds should use a documented exact SDK acquisition path.

javascript.mixing_risk: No pnpm, Yarn, or Bun lockfiles found.

runtime_dependencies: Qdrant 1.17.1 native Windows payload from packaging manifest
PaddleOCR 3.5.0 and selected PaddlePaddle runtime for OCR provisioning
suspicious_or_sensitive_packages_to_revi: Python OCR GPU packages from PaddlePaddle extra indexes
Bundled native qdrant.exe downloaded from GitHub release asset
version_inconsistencies_to_resolve: CI Node selection uses lts/* while package.json allows ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0; choose and enforce the production Node major/version.
CI .NET selection uses 10.0.x while global.json pins 10.0.300 with roll-forward; document whether release builds must use exactly 10.0.300 or feature roll-forward.
package.json uses semver ranges; production must rely on package-lock.json and npm ci.
